c.tagline: Silk Road oasis and China's best-preserved Islamic old city, gateway to the Pamirs.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are metered; short trips are cheap, but agreeing a price or using Didi is common for longer or out-of-town rides. Carry your destination written in Chinese.

emergency.note: 110 reaches the police and 120 reaches medical/ambulance services; 119 is the fire brigade.

solo.f: generally fine; expect heavy security presence

avoid.reason: Xinjiang — heavy security, checkpoints and surveillance; restrictions on movement/photography; check advisories

hood_desc: The famous Kashgar Old Town (Ancient City), a labyrinth of mud-brick Uyghur houses, artisan workshops, teahouses, and lanes that has been a Silk Road crossroads for over two millennia; best for first-timers who want to stay amid the sights.
The city-center square in front of the yellow-tiled Id Kah Mosque, the spiritual heart of Kashgar, surrounded by shops, eateries, and mid-range hotels; a convenient, well-connected base.
The downtown stretch along Renmin Road, the modern commercial spine with department stores, banks, restaurants, and larger hotels; a practical, central place to stay.
The district around the Grand (Sunday) Bazaar and the Ostangboyi craft street, busiest on Sundays with carpets, spices, copperware, and livestock nearby; ideal for shoppers and market-goers.
The quieter East Lake (Donghu) Park area on the city's edge, with waterfront parkland and newer hotels away from the crowds; a calmer, greener base.

water.note: Drink bottled or boiled water only.

transit.hours: City buses generally run from around 7:00 AM to 9:00-10:00 PM; taxis and ride-hailing fill the late-evening gap.
transit.note: Kashgar has no metro or tram; getting around relies on an extensive city bus network plus cheap, plentiful taxis. The compact Old Town and central sights are easily walkable.
transit.pay: Buses take a rechargeable transit card, mobile QR payment (Alipay/WeChat), or cash; taxis are paid in cash or by app.

bus: Long-distance coaches across southern Xinjiang and to the Karakoram Highway

car.idp: Not valid; a temporary Chinese license is required to drive

train: Kashgar Railway Station (Southern Xinjiang Railway services to Ürümqi and intermediate cities)

transit.m: Airport bus / city bus to the center (~30-40 min)

tip.r: Tipping is not customary or expected in restaurants, taxis, or hotels.

food.name: Laghman
food.desc: Hand-pulled wheat noodles topped with stir-fried lamb, peppers, tomato and garlic chives; the everyday meal of every Uyghur household.

places.name: Ostangboyi Food Street
places.note: The old city's main eating street, where noodle masters pull dough to order in open kitchens.

places.name: Kashgar Night Market
places.note: Dozens of stalls firing up at dusk; the easiest place to point at what you want.

places.name: Kashgar Grand Bazaar food stalls
places.note: Bazaar canteens feeding traders all day, with laghman and suoman at low prices.

food.name: Polo (Uyghur Pilaf)
food.desc: Rice slow-cooked in lamb fat and broth with carrot, onion and raisins, crowned with a piece of bone-in mutton.

places.name: Sunday Livestock Market stalls
places.area: Yengi Sheher, north of the city
places.note: Enormous cauldrons feed the traders from dawn; the most atmospheric polo in Kashgar.

places.name: Old Town food bazaar
places.note: Sells smaller portions of polo, useful if you want to taste several dishes.

places.name: Ostangboyi Food Street
places.note: Polo shops here open early and often sell out by mid-morning, so go for breakfast.

food.name: Samsa
food.desc: Square pastries stuffed with diced lamb, onion, cumin and pepper, slapped onto the wall of a clay tandoor and baked until blistered.

places.name: Id Kah Mosque Square stalls
places.note: Tandoor ovens right on the square turn out samsa all day; eat them standing and hot.

places.name: Ostangboyi Food Street
places.note: Bakers here work clay ovens set into the wall, so you can watch the samsa go in.

places.name: Kashgar Grand Bazaar
places.note: Cheap, fast bazaar samsa for eating on the move between stalls.

food.name: Nan
food.desc: Round tandoor-baked flatbread stamped with a patterned nan skewer and studded with onion and sesame; eaten with every meal.

places.name: Nan bakeries, Ostangboyi Road
places.note: Family bakeries with tandoors sunk into the floor, baking from before sunrise.

places.name: Old Town lanes near Id Kah
places.note: Small neighborhood ovens sell nan by the piece straight off the oven wall.

places.name: Kashgar Grand Bazaar
places.note: Stacks of nan in every size, including the thick girde and the huge thin sheets.

food.name: Kawap (Lamb Kebabs)
food.desc: Chunks of fat-laced lamb threaded on iron skewers, dusted with cumin and chilli and grilled over charcoal until the edges char.

places.name: Kashgar Night Market
places.note: The city's kebab headquarters after dark, with smoke visible from the mosque square.

places.name: Ostangboyi Food Street
places.note: Charcoal grills line the street; the whole-lamb and rib versions are worth seeking out.

places.name: Sunday Livestock Market stalls
places.note: Kebabs grilled beside the sheep pens; as fresh as lamb gets.

food.name: Goshnan
food.desc: A large flat meat pie of lamb and onion sealed between two rounds of dough and pan-fried in a shallow pan, sliced into wedges.

places.name: Ostangboyi Food Street
places.note: Shops with wide flat pans out front, cutting goshnan into wedges as it comes off the heat.

places.name: Kashgar Night Market
places.note: Evening stalls make goshnan to order; ask for a quarter if you are eating several things.

places.name: Old Town food bazaar
places.note: Daytime option for goshnan and other pan-fried Uyghur breads.

food.name: Atken Chay (Uyghur Milk Tea)
food.desc: Brick tea boiled with milk, salt and sometimes butter or cream, drunk from a bowl with torn nan dipped into it.

places.name: Ostangboyi Ancient Teahouse
places.note: The century-old teahouse above the street, full of old men, music and endless pots of tea.

places.name: Old Town teahouses
places.note: Small upstairs rooms all over the old quarter where tea comes with bread and conversation.

places.name: Kashgar Grand Bazaar tea stalls
places.note: Traders' tea counters serving milk tea and dogh through the market day.

food.name: Fresh Pomegranate Juice
food.desc: Deep red juice pressed to order from Xinjiang pomegranates on hand-cranked presses; tart, cold and sold by the cup all over town.

places.name: Juice carts, Id Kah Square
places.note: Rows of presses in front of the mosque, pressing the fruit while you wait.

places.name: Ostangboyi Food Street
places.note: Juice stands sit between the kebab grills, ideal after something heavy and cumin-heavy.

places.name: Kashgar Grand Bazaar
places.note: Also the place to buy the dried fruit and mulberries Kashgar is known for.

landmarks: Id Kah Mosque
China's largest mosque, a yellow-tiled 15th-century landmark whose leafy courtyards have anchored Uyghur religious life on Kashgar's central square for centuries.
Kashgar Old City
A living labyrinth of mud-brick alleys, carved balconies and artisan workshops, this ancient Silk Road quarter feels like stepping back a thousand years.
Kashgar Grand (Sunday) Bazaar
Central Asia's most storied market heaves with carpets, spices, silks and knives, carrying on two millennia of Silk Road trading tradition.
Afaq Khoja Mausoleum
A serene 17th-century tiled mausoleum complex holding five generations of a powerful Sufi family, revered as Xinjiang's holiest Islamic site.
Sunday Livestock Market
Uyghur farmers haggle over sheep, camels and donkeys in a raucous weekly spectacle that remains one of Asia's great authentic market experiences.
Gaotai Ancient Homes
Perched on a loess cliff above the Tuman River, this 600-year-old stack of mud-brick Uyghur houses is Kashgar's most evocative photographic subject.
Handicraft Street (Ostangboyi)
Coppersmiths hammer teapots and instrument makers carve rawaps along this atmospheric artisan lane, where Kashgar's craft traditions survive in open-fronted workshops.
Mor Pagoda (Mo'er Buddhist Stupa)
Crumbling remains of a 7th-century Buddhist stupa and temple outside the city testify to Kashgar's pre-Islamic role on the Buddhist Silk Road.
Shipton's Arch (Tushuk Tash)
A day trip into the Kara Tagh mountains reveals possibly the world's tallest natural arch, a 365-metre stone gateway hidden in sheer canyons.
Karakul Lake
Along the fabled Karakoram Highway, this glacial lake mirrors 7,546-metre Muztagh Ata, delivering the most spectacular day trip in Chinese Central Asia.

train.note: There is no cross-border passenger railway from Kashgar - rail links to Osh in Kyrgyzstan and over the Khunjerab Pass to Pakistan have been discussed for decades but none has been built, so every international journey starts on the road. Kashgar station is the westernmost railway station in China and is the terminus of the Southern Xinjiang Railway: trains run to Urumqi in roughly 25 hours and, on the Kashgar-Hotan line, to Hotan in about 10 hours. Buy tickets on 12306 or at the station with your passport, and allow extra time for the airport-style security and identity checks that apply across Xinjiang.

intl.to: Osh & Bishkek (Kyrgyzstan) via the Irkeshtam and Torugart passes
intl.op: cross-border coaches from Kashgar International Bus Station — counter sales only, no online booking

intl.to: Sost & Gilgit (Pakistan) via the Khunjerab Pass on the Karakoram Highway
intl.op: seasonal cross-border coaches from Kashgar International Bus Station — counter sales only, no online booking

bus.note: International coaches leave from the international bus station rather than the regional one, and tickets are sold over the counter a day or two ahead - there is no online booking, and a valid onward visa is checked before you board. The Kyrgyz routes go over the Irkeshtam pass (the more reliable of the two, for Osh) or the Torugart pass, which is a controlled crossing where travellers are usually required to be met by a pre-arranged vehicle on the far side. The Karakoram Highway to Sost and Gilgit in Pakistan is only open in the warmer months, typically around May to October, and closes for snow and for Chinese and Pakistani public holidays, so confirm locally before committing. All crossings involve long waits at Chinese customs at Ulugqat or Tashkurgan, and Xinjiang time is two hours ahead of the unofficial local clock, which regularly catches people out.

ferry.note: Kashgar sits in the Tarim Basin at the western edge of the Taklamakan Desert, about as far from any ocean as it is possible to be, and there are no navigable rivers or lakes nearby - no passenger boat services exist.

half.name: Yengisar
half.blurb: Craftsmen have forged decorative Uyghur knives with inlaid handles in this town for roughly 400 years.

full.name: Tashkurgan Stone Fortress
full.blurb: Mud-brick fortress ruins overlook a high grassland valley near the Pakistan border, once a stop on the Silk Road's Pamir crossing.
